items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install Clients)
items.preview:
**Why this wins:** 30 freshly-installed, satisfied clients still in the honeymoon window. No service plan pitch allowed (they're under 1 year), and no review asks allowed, so referrals are the natural and highest-value ask. Dollar amounts are concrete and convert.
**1. Campaign name + audience size**
`Referral Program - New Client Honeymoon Window` | **30 members**
**2. Subject line (60 char max) + alternates**
- **Primary:** `Know someone drinking bad water?` (pain)
- Alt 1: `$500 for a two-minute favor` (specific)
- Alt 2: `The quiet thing most of our clients do next` (curiosity)
- Alt 3: `We built this on neighbors telling neighbors` (authority)
- Alt 4: `Your water is handled. Who's next?` (curiosity/specific)
**3. Preview text (90 char max)**
`A name and a number is all it takes. Here is exactly what it is worth to you.`
**4. Email body draft**
> Hi {First Name},
>
> It's been about a month since we installed your ClearWave system, and by now the water should just feel like a non-issue. That's the goal: you stop thinking about it.
>
> Here's the one ask we make of happy clients. If you know someone fighting hard water, staining, or water they don't trust, send them our way for a free water assessment.
>
> Here's what it's worth to you:
>
> - If they become a client: $500 cash. (It climbs to $750 after your fifth referral this year, and $1,000 once you hit ten.)
> - If they just book a consult: a $50 gift card, win or lose.
>
> No pressure, no quota. Just reply with a name and a number, or send them straight to us.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
**5. Send timing**
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET.** Mid-morning Tuesday is the cleanest open window; avoids Monday inbox pileup and keeps it away from the fatigued weekend blast pattern.
**6. Expected performance**
- **Open: 44-48%.** Above the 42.3% baseline. These are recent, warm installs (vs. the whole stale 3,659 list), and the subject is client-benefit, not the "course IS LIVE" internal-sounding copy that tanked to 0.4%.
- **Click: 3-5%.** Massive lift over the 0.28% average because there's a real, personal, dollar-denominated reason to engage (prior campaigns had no genuine client payoff).
- **Conversion (referral submitted): 6-10% (2-3 referrals).** Honeymoon-window clients are most likely to advocate; even one closed referral returns $500 against near-zero send cost.
**7. Source justification**
Draws from the **Referral push candidates (30-60 days post-install, satisfied)** Jobber trigger (30 contacts). Uses exact **Referral Bonus Structure** numbers. Respects Hard Rule 1 (no service pitch pre-12-month), Hard Rule 3 (referral not review), and Hard Rule 3a ("free water assessment"). Product names withheld per Hard Rule 2 (all 30 systems carry legacy names like "H2O Protector," "Re-Ionator Pro Ultra," "30c"), so the blanket tenure line is used instead.
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge "Is It Worth It?" (13-24 Month Clients)
items.preview:
**Why this wins:** 100 clients, all past their year-1 service (so Concierge is allowed and they already trust the service experience). This is the largest qualified segment and carries recurring-revenue upside ($99/mo). The non-pushy "here's the math" framing is tailor-made for a list showing fatigue toward hard-sell subject lines.
**1. Campaign name + audience size**
`Concierge: The Year 1.5 Question` | **100 members**
**2. Subject line (60 char max) + alternates**
- **Primary:** `The question we get at the 18-month mark` (curiosity)
- Alt 1: `Is Concierge actually worth it? Let's do the math` (specific)
- Alt 2: `Filters, parts, service: who's tracking yours?` (pain)
- Alt 3: `$99 a month, and here's exactly what's in it` (specific/authority)
- Alt 4: `You're past year one. One thing to consider.` (curiosity)
**3. Preview text (90 char max)**
`No pressure. Just the honest math on whether this makes sense for your home.`
**4. Email body draft**
> Hi {First Name},
>
> It's been about a year and a half since we installed your water system, which means you've had your first annual service and you know how we work.
>
> Around this point we get one question a lot: "Is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?" Fair question. Here's the honest math.
>
> Concierge is $99/month and covers:
>
> - Your annual service, done without you having to remember it
> - Filter swaps on schedule
> - Priority phone support when you call
> - Parts coverage on your standard install components
>
> If you're the type who'd rather it just be handled, it pays for itself in peace of mind alone. If you prefer pay-as-you-go, that's completely fine too. No wrong answer.
>
> Want me to run the numbers for your specific setup? Just reply and I'll send them over.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
**5. Send timing**
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET.** Spaces it two days from the referral send so the two campaigns don't collide in anyone's inbox, and keeps a consistent mid-morning weekday rhythm.
**6. Expected performance**
- **Open: 40-45%.** Around baseline. Slightly lower than Proposal 1 because the segment is older (13-24 mo) and the recurring-charge topic is weightier, but the curiosity-framed subject beats the dead "Discount Ends Today" pattern.
- **Click: 1-2.5%.** Strong lift over 0.28% baseline; the "reply and I'll run your numbers" soft CTA lowers friction vs. a hard buy button.
- **Conversion (Concierge signup or reply): 2-4% (2-4 signups).** At $99/mo, even 3 signups is ~$3,500/yr recurring. These clients have already experienced the service, which is the strongest predictor of plan adoption.
**7. Source justification**
Draws from the **Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months, not on Concierge)** Jobber trigger (100 contacts) and the **Concierge Upsell Context** block (exact $99/mo scope and the "is it worth it at year 1.5" framing). Honors Hard Rule 1 (all candidates are already past 12 months, list is pre-filtered). Product names are withheld per Hard Rule 2 since the sample systems carry legacy/unspecified names; blanket tenure line used. "Free water assessment" phrasing not needed here (existing clients, not prospects).
---
### Sequencing note
Run **Proposal 1 Tuesday**, **Proposal 2 Thursday**. Different audiences (zero overlap: 30-60 day vs. 13-24 month), so no fatigue risk, and both move away from the hard-sell subject lines that drove recent opens to ~0.5%.
